picks.style: ancient greek hymn-chorus, bowed lyre, deep drone, layered women's voices, slow, awed, spacious
picks.why: The hymn to an unsearchable Zeus — 'the pathways of his understanding stretch dark and tangled' — one voice, one thought, complete.

picks.style: tragic lament, aulos, low frame drum, keening female voices, slow then agitated, desolate
picks.why: The maidens would rather hang, or fall from a vulture-haunted crag, than be married — terror in concrete images.

picks.style: greek processional chorus, lyre, hand drum, unison female voices, steady walking pulse, hypnotic
picks.why: Io driven by the gadfly across Phrygia, Lydia, Cilicia and the wheat-lands of Aphrodite — a place-name litany that moves.

picks.style: greek chorus of furies, aulos, rattles, low drum, layered whispering-to-shrieking female voices, urgent, unnerving
picks.why: 'You goddesses swiftly careering on your wings, whose lot it is to hold a revel, not with Bacchic rites, in tears and groans.'

picks.style: tragic prologue, solo lyre, sparse drone, grave female voice, slow, weary, direct address
picks.why: Electra opening the play with Tantalus quailing beneath his rock — the whole cursed house named in one speech.

picks.style: greek monody, kithara, low strings, soaring then breaking female voice, slow, ominous, cosmic
picks.why: The golden lamb, and Strife turning the sun's chariot back toward the dawn — the myth at its strangest and most vivid.

picks.style: nordic ballad, nyckelharpa, bowed lyre, frame drum, fierce female voice, incantatory, cold, gathering
picks.why: 'Argantyr, wake! — to thee I call, / Hear from thy dark sepulchral hall!' — a daughter raising her father from the grave.

picks.style: norse incantation, low drone, war drum, hard female chant with male answering voice, driving, repetitive, blazing
picks.why: 'Scorns the car... scorns the helmet, scorns the spear' — repetition built for chanting, and the sword demanded from a dead hand.

picks.style: nordic lullaby for the dead, bowed strings, soft drum, low female voice, very slow, hushed, restorative
picks.why: 'Sleep, Argantyr, — Chief of might, / Thro' the long, the dreary night' — the closing of the tomb; a natural song's ending.

picks.style: abolitionist anthem, chamber organ, low strings, grave female voice with chorus, slow, indignant, building
picks.why: 'Sense is as keen where Congo's sons preside, / As where proud Tiber rolls his classic tide' — the argument at its sharpest.

picks.style: protest lament, cello, sparse piano, anguished mezzo, slow, unflinching
picks.why: The burning village, the shrieking babe, the wife dragged off — 'the fibres twisting round a parent's heart... bleeding as they part'.

picks.style: 18th century satirical air, harpsichord, oboe, arch light tenor, brisk, drawing-room wit
picks.why: 'Small habits, well pursued betimes, / May reach the dignity of crimes' — the whole poem's comic method in two lines.

picks.style: balinese kidung chant, gender wayang gamelan, suling flute, male chant, slow, ceremonial, incense-heavy
picks.why: The opening benediction and oṁ namaḥ śivāya, then the five yamas and niyamas laid out cleanly — a proper invocation.

picks.style: kawi didactic chant, metallophone, small gong, steady male voice, measured, instructive, two-part answering shape
picks.why: The undisciplined child who shames his father set against the disciplined one who honours him — a built-in parallel structure.

picks.style: javanese-balinese devotional chant, gamelan drone, kendang, unison male voices, slow, serene
picks.why: The tenfold mark of dharma closing on the ascetic whose bearing is as constant as sun and moon, day and night.

picks.style: russian revolutionary song, accordion, balalaika, ragged male chorus, marching, raw, defiant
picks.why: Blok's 'At Holy Russia let's fire a shot... eh, eh, unhallowed, unblessed' beside words settling like halcyon birds on branches.

picks.style: english romantic art song, piano, cello, dark baritone, slow, sombre, resigned
picks.why: Shelley on the wise wanting love and the loving wanting wisdom, 'and all best things are thus confused to ill' — whole and quotable.

picks.style: pindaric victory ode, kithara, aulos, bright male voice with small chorus, stately, radiant, ceremonial
picks.why: Pindar's opening — water best of all things, gold blazing like fire in the night — the most famous line in Greek lyric.
